questions.q:
A is the point (−3, 2) and B is the point (5, −4).
Find the gradient of the line AB.
questions.tip: Keep the same order on the top and the bottom: (y₂ − y₁) ÷ (x₂ − x₁).

questions.q:
The equation of a line is 3y − 6x = 7.
(a) Find the gradient of the line. [1]
(b) Write down the equation of the line parallel to 3y − 6x = 7 which passes through (0, −1). [1]
questions.model:
(a) 3y = 6x + 7 → y = 2x + 7/3, so the gradient is 2.
(b) Same gradient, y-intercept −1: y = 2x − 1.
questions.tip: Rearrange to y = mx + c before reading the gradient: it is not 6 or −6.

questions.q:
P is the point (−2, 1) and Q is the point (4, 9).
(a) Calculate the length of PQ. [2]
(b) Q is the midpoint of the line PR. Find the coordinates of R. [2]
ms: (b) M1: one correct coordinate of R, or (x − 2)/2 = 4 or (y + 1)/2 = 9
questions.model:
(a) Horizontal change 6, vertical change 8. PQ = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10.
(b) From P to Q: +6 across, +8 up. Do the same again from Q: R = (4 + 6, 9 + 8) = (10, 17).
questions.tip: Q is the midpoint, so R is the same step beyond Q as Q is beyond P.

questions.q:
(a) Find the equation of the line through (−1, 7) and (3, −1). Give your answer in the form y = mx + c. [3]
(b) Find the coordinates of the point where this line crosses the x-axis. [1]
ms: (a) M1: substitutes a point into y = their m x + c, e.g. 7 = −2(−1) + c
questions.tip: Check your line with the second point: −2(3) + 5 = −1 ✓.

questions.q:
A is the point (0, 4), B is the point (6, 0) and C is the point (8, 3).
(a) Use gradients to show that angle ABC = 90°. [3]
(b) Calculate the area of triangle ABC. [2]
(c) Find the equation of the line AC. Give your answer in the form ax + by = c, where a, b and c are integers. [3]
ms: (a) A1: product = −1 (or one is the negative reciprocal of the other), so AB is perpendicular to BC
(b) M1: ½ × √52 × √13 oe (or rectangle minus triangles method)
(c) M1: y = −x/8 + 4 or substitutes a point correctly
questions.model:
(a) Gradient AB = (0 − 4) ÷ 6 = −2/3. Gradient BC = (3 − 0) ÷ (8 − 6) = 3/2.
−2/3 × 3/2 = −1, so AB is perpendicular to BC and angle ABC = 90°.
(b) AB = √(36 + 16) = √52, BC = √(4 + 9) = √13.
Area = ½ × √52 × √13 = ½ × √676 = ½ × 26 = 13 square units.
(c) Gradient AC = (3 − 4) ÷ 8 = −1/8. y = −x/8 + 4.
Multiply by 8: 8y = −x + 32, so x + 8y = 32.
questions.tip: Because angle B is 90°, AB and BC are the base and height of the triangle.

questions.q:
Line L₁ has equation y = 3x − 5. Line L₂ has equation x + 2y = 11.
(a) Find the coordinates of P, the point where L₁ and L₂ intersect. [3]
(b) Find the equation of the line through P that is perpendicular to L₁. Give your answer in the form y = mx + c. [3]
questions.model:
(a) x + 2(3x − 5) = 11 → 7x − 10 = 11 → x = 3. y = 3(3) − 5 = 4. P(3, 4).
(b) Gradient of L₁ is 3, so the perpendicular gradient is −1/3.
4 = −1/3 × 3 + c → c = 5. y = −x/3 + 5.
questions.tip: Perpendicular gradient: flip and change the sign (3 → −1/3).
